---

## What is Claude Code? 🤖

- An AI assistant that works directly in your project
- Runs in the terminal (and inside VS Code)
- It can read your files, change them and run commands (including `git`)
- It asks for your permission before changing files or running commands

## Starting Claude Code

Open the terminal in your repository and run:

```bash
claude
```

Then just describe what you want it to do, e.g.

```text
Add a section to the README explaining what this repository is about
```

## Claude Code & git: Use a Branch 🌳

- Let Claude Code work on its own branch, not on `main`
  - Its changes stay separate until you reviewed them
  - If you don't like the result, you can simply delete the branch

::: {.fragment}
```bash
git checkout -b claude-readme
# Switched to a new branch 'claude-readme'
```
:::

## Reviewing the Changes 🔍

- Treat changes by Claude Code just like changes by a colleague
- Before committing, look at what actually changed
  - `git status` to see which files were changed
  - `git diff` (or VS Code) to see the changes line by line
- Then commit, push and create a merge request as usual

::: {.fragment}
:::{.callout-important}
You are responsible for what you merge, not the AI assistant!
:::
:::

## Working with Claude Code: Tips 💡

- Be specific about what you want
- Keep changes small, so they are easy to review
- Ask Claude Code to explain changes you don't understand
- Never share passwords, keys or sensitive data with it

# Demo: Claude Code on a Branch

## Practical: Claude Code on a Branch {background-color="black"}

1. Go back to your Terminal in `git-exercise`
2. Create a new branch called `claude-code` and check it out
3. Start Claude Code with `claude` and ask it to make a change (e.g. improve your `README`)
4. Review the changes with `git status` and `git diff`
5. Commit the changes and push the branch to GitLab
6. Create a merge request and review the changes there once more
7. Merge (or close) the merge request

:::{.callout-note}
No access to Claude Code? Pair up with someone who has access.
:::
